questions.q: Describe the Fundamental Rights guaranteed by the Indian Constitution.
answer: The Constitution guarantees six Fundamental Rights that the government cannot take away.

answer.text: The Right to Equality ensures equality before the law, forbids discrimination, and abolishes untouchability. The Right to Freedom gives freedom of speech, assembly, movement, residence and profession, and protects personal liberty.
The Right against Exploitation bans forced labour, child labour and human trafficking, while the Right to Freedom of Religion allows everyone to follow, practise and propagate any religion.

Cultural and Educational Rights let minorities preserve their culture and run their own institutions, and the Right to Constitutional Remedies allows citizens to approach the courts to enforce these rights.

questions.q: Why did Dr Ambedkar call the Right to Constitutional Remedies the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution?
answer: Dr B.R. Ambedkar described the Right to Constitutional Remedies as the heart and soul of the Constitution because it gives life to all the other rights.

answer.text: A right written in the Constitution is of little use unless there is a way to enforce it. This right ensures that if any Fundamental Right is violated, the citizen can act.
Under it, a citizen can go directly to the Supreme Court or a High Court, which can issue writs — such as habeas corpus and mandamus — to protect the right and order the government to act lawfully.
Because it makes every other Fundamental Right real and enforceable, without it the rest would be mere words, which is why Ambedkar gave it this special place.

questions.q: How do Fundamental Duties complement Fundamental Rights in the Constitution?

answer.text: were added to the Constitution to remind citizens that rights come with responsibilities towards the nation and one another.

list: They include respecting the Constitution, the national flag and anthem, and defending the country when called upon
They ask citizens to promote harmony, protect the environment and public property, and value our composite culture

answer.text: Rights and duties are two sides of citizenship.

list: While rights protect the individual, duties call on individuals to strengthen the community and the country
Though not legally enforced like rights, they set a moral standard for good citizenship
